wausau pd.name: Wausau Police Department
wausau pd.note: 20 cameras at 11 locations under a five-year, $250,000 sole-source contract approved in October 2023 and running to December 2028. The agreement has no early termination for convenience, though a non-appropriation clause lets the city leave without penalty on 30 days' notice if funds are not budgeted; as of the report, Mayor Doug Diny had not said whether the 2027 budget includes the December payment. The department turned off nationwide sharing in May 2026 and now shares only with Wisconsin agencies. Its policy requires annual written audits; it has produced three, each reviewing 10 searches out of more than 10,000 a year. The contract gives Flock perpetual rights to use de-identified data in its other products. Current camera and search figures are from its transparency portal, above.

portal.prohibited_uses: Immigration enforcement, harassment or intimidation, actions based solely on a protected class (such as race, sex, or religion), and any personal use.

marathon county so.name: Marathon County Sheriff's Office
marathon county so.note: Sheriff Chad Billeb has said he will keep the office's 10 Flock cameras as other Wisconsin agencies cover or cancel theirs. The cameras cost $26,500 a year and have been grant-funded since 2023; the contract lets the county leave at any time for $500 a camera, about $4,000, with a prorated refund. Shares its data with more than 1,400 agencies in 40 states, including seven federal agencies, and joined ICE's 287(g) jail-enforcement program in late 2025. Its policy says command staff "may" audit searches, with no schedule and no written findings required; asked by a county supervisor whether that could become "shall," a captain said the change could be made. Current figures are from its transparency portal, above.

waupaca county so.name: Waupaca County Sheriff's Office
waupaca county so.note: The county's Law Enforcement Committee voted to cut Flock funding from next year's budget, and the sheriff then suspended the cameras, citing loss of control over sensitive law enforcement information. The county spent $34,500 on Flock this year. Law enforcement agencies across the county announced the suspension jointly on Sept. 8.

stevens point pd.name: Stevens Point Police Department
stevens point pd.note: Mayor Mike Wiza had the city's 10 Flock cameras covered and suspended their use, citing doubts about how the company uses camera data and possible misuse by outsiders. The city is exploring ending the contract; no termination has been reported.

grand chute pd.name: Grand Chute Police Department
grand chute pd.note: Town Board voted unanimously on June 2 to end its Flock contracts, the police chief citing cameras down for months and harder oversight of outside access. The town is keeping plate readers: its 23 cameras were to be replaced with Axon's by Sept. 1.

kaukauna pd.name: Kaukauna Police Department
kaukauna pd.note: Did not renew its three-year Flock contract for six cameras when it expired in June 2026; the police chief said continuing was not fiscally responsible given the concerns raised.

de pere pd.name: De Pere Police Department
de pere pd.note: Police chief announced an immediate end to officers' use of Flock cameras on Sept. 14, citing data disclosed without authorization. Cameras are bagged until the contract expires Nov. 15, 2026; the report does not say whether it will be renewed.

jefferson county so.name: Jefferson County Sheriff's Office
jefferson county so.note: Sheriff suspended use of the cameras on Sept. 10 after learning that data on cases the office investigated in 2025 had been made public without its consent. No contract decision was reported.

clark county so.name: Clark County Sheriff's Office
clark county so.note: Sheriff Kerry Kirn announced on Sept. 17 that the office notified Flock on Sept. 10 it was cancelling its contract and ending plate-reader use countywide, citing residents' privacy concerns.

university of milwaukee pd.name: University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee Police Department
university of milwaukee pd.note: Ended its use of Flock and directed the company to remove all 18 campus cameras, plus two nearby; they are bagged in the meantime. Parking-facility plate readers are a separate system and are not affected.

cottage grove pd.name: Cottage Grove Police Department
cottage grove pd.note: Village Board voted unanimously on Sept. 21 to stop using Flock and deactivate the village's nine cameras immediately, and directed staff to draft an ordinance barring the village from using plate-reader technology of any brand.

waunakee pd.name: Waunakee Police Department
waunakee pd.note: Police chief removed the village's five Flock cameras in mid-September after they were damaged in August and September. The contract expires at year's end and the chief is evaluating other plate-reader vendors; no decision on the Flock contract reported.

oneida county so.name: Oneida County Sheriff's Office
oneida county so.note: Sheriff Grady Hartman ended the office's use of Flock plate readers, citing public opposition and the potential for abuse. The chief deputy said the cameras had been offline since the end of August and were being taken down.

manitowoc pd.name: Manitowoc Police Department
manitowoc pd.note: Mayor Justin Nickels said the city will not renew its Flock contract and asked Flock to remove its cameras, which the city had deactivated on Sept. 5. The city budget will not fund plate-reader cameras.

mcfarland pd.name: McFarland Police Department
mcfarland pd.note: Called off a planned Flock purchase, budgeted for 2026, before buying any cameras, citing Dane County's loss of Flock funding and residents' privacy concerns. It still appears in other agencies' Flock sharing lists.

deforest pd.name: DeForest Police Department
deforest pd.note: Police Chief James Olson, vice president of the Wisconsin Police Chiefs Association, has said his department does not have Flock cameras. It still appears in other agencies' Flock sharing lists, and USA TODAY's records show it has run searches on the network, which does not require cameras of its own.

lake mills pd.name: Lake Mills Police Department
lake mills pd.note: Police Chief Steve Schroeder said the department is opting out of its Flock contract after its search data was shared outside the agency without authorization; the cameras stay covered until Flock removes them.

kenosha pd.name: Kenosha Police Department
kenosha pd.note: Mayor David Bogdala and Police Chief Patrick Patton said the city is ending its Flock contract a year early, citing data-security concerns and eroding trust, and replacing the cameras with Axon plate readers the department owns, limiting sharing to Wisconsin agencies and possibly Lake County, Ill. It still runs plate readers, just not Flock's.

marinette pd.name: Marinette Police Department
marinette pd.note: Common Council voted 9-0 on Sept. 17 to end the city's Flock contract. The mayor and police chief had ordered the cameras covered weeks earlier while the service was reviewed.

wautoma pd.name: Wautoma Police Department
wautoma pd.note: Police Chief Paul Mott told the Common Council on Sept. 14 that the department had canceled its Flock contract.

ashland pd.name: Ashland Police Department
ashland pd.note: Police Chief Brandon Marten said the department would not renew its one-year Flock contract and would remove the cameras, citing frequent downtime, slow service from Flock and community concerns.
